title: Super-Imperialism
author: Michael Hudson
desc: EE.UU. usa el sistema financiero como arma imperial. El dólar como instrumento de dominación global.
tesis: Estados Unidos creó un tipo de imperialismo sin precedentes: no cobra tributo en oro ni coloniza territorios — obliga al mundo entero a financiar su déficit comprando bonos del Tesoro denominados en dólares que nunca pagará en valor real. Desde que Nixon abandonó el patrón oro en 1971, EE.UU. exporta dólares (que puede imprimir sin límite) e importa bienes reales. Los países del mundo, especialmente Asia y los exportadores de petróleo, acumulan reservas en dólares que reciclan comprando deuda estadounidense — financiando así el gasto militar que los mantiene subordinados. Es un tributo imperial disfrazado de sistema financiero internacional.
ideas: El dólar como moneda de reserva mundial es el mecanismo imperial más eficiente de la historia: EE.UU. imprime dinero, el mundo entrega bienes reales.
Desde 1971, el sistema monetario internacional funciona como tributo: los superávits comerciales del mundo se reciclan como préstamos a EE.UU. que financian su presupuesto militar.
El FMI y el Banco Mundial no son instituciones neutrales — son instrumentos de la política económica estadounidense para imponer austeridad y privatización en la periferia.
La 'deuda del Tercer Mundo' es un mecanismo de control: los países pobres pagan intereses perpetuos por préstamos que beneficiaron a las corporaciones del centro.
La desdolarización (BRICS, yuan, comercio bilateral) es la mayor amenaza al imperio estadounidense — más que cualquier ejército.
contexto: Originalmente publicado en 1972, justo después de que Nixon abandonara el patrón oro (agosto 1971). Hudson, economista de Wall Street, había asesorado al gobierno canadiense sobre flujos de capital. La tercera edición (2021) actualiza el análisis con la crisis financiera de 2008, las sanciones a Rusia y el ascenso de China. Irónicamente, el Pentágono fue uno de los primeros compradores del libro en 1972 — lo usaron como manual de operaciones.
porqueLeer: Porque explica por qué el dólar es la base del poder estadounidense y por qué la desdolarización es el campo de batalla geopolítico del siglo XXI. Es el libro que mejor conecta las finanzas internacionales con el imperialismo. Después de leerlo, frases como 'libre mercado' y 'estabilidad financiera' nunca suenan igual.

conexiones.razon: Lenin analizó el imperialismo del capital financiero; Hudson lo actualiza al imperialismo del dólar como moneda de reserva.
Galeano documentó el saqueo colonial; Hudson explica el mecanismo financiero del saqueo contemporáneo.
Parenti documenta las intervenciones militares; Hudson revela el brazo financiero del mismo imperio.
...and Forgive Them Their Debts analiza la deuda en la antigüedad; Super-Imperialism la analiza en el presente.

deck.label: NotebookLM briefing — The American Debtor Empire

quotes.text: America has run rings around Britain and every other empire-making nation in history. It has been the most successful empire the world has ever seen — in part because it has convinced the world it is not an empire at all.

At the root of this new form of imperialism is the exploitation of countries and their governments by a single government, that of the United States, more via the central banks and multilateral control institutions of inter-governmental capital than by the activities of private corporations seeking profits.

What has turned the older forms of colonialist imperialism into an American super-imperialism is that whereas prior to the 1960s the U.S. Government dominated international organizations by virtue of its preeminent creditor status, since that time it has done so by virtue of its debtor position.

The key to understanding today's dollar standard is to see that it has become a debt standard based on U.S. Treasury IOUs, not on assets in the form of gold bullion. While applying creditor-oriented rules against Third World countries, the Washington Consensus promotes domestic U.S. credit expansion untrammeled by America's own deepening trade deficit.

tl: U.S. enters WWI as creditor, extending $12 billion in Inter-Ally loans

The nation declared war in 1917 only when it became apparent that to stay out would entail at least an interim economic collapse. American bankers and exporters faced the threat of being stuck with uncollectible loans to Britain and its allies
Versalles y la deuda inter-gubernamental
the world economy emerged from World War I shackled with debts far... by British industry. After World War I the U.S. Government pursued... onerous Treaty of Versailles imposed on Germany
Crash de Wall Street y la deuda envenenada

America's holding down its interest rates vis-a-vis those of Britain worked to inflate the stock market bubble that burst in 1929. The Great Depression extinguished private capital throughout the world
Roosevelt torpedoes London Economic Conference; devalues the dollar

The United States had rejected this fixed gold-value currency principle at the 1933 World Economic Conference in London. The U.S. motive at that time was to devalue the dollar relative to all other currencies
Bretton Woods y el triunfo del capital financiero estatal
In July 1944 the IMF and World Bank were established at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, as permanent financial and... Bretton Woods institutions cloaked the Anglo-American key-currency
El Prestamo Britanico desmantela el Area Esterlina
with its overvalued pound sterling, having waived its right to devalue or protect its Sterling Area in exchange for receiving the 1946 British Loan from the U.S. Treasury
Plan Marshall: ayuda para abrir mercados

Marshall Plan Aid during 1948-51. It took the initiative in forming the United Nations and the Bretton Woods institutions to ward off a renewal... This red specter was what had turned the tide on the British Loan, and it carried Marshall Plan Aid
Golpes en Iran y Guatemala
Iran's desire to control its own oil and Guatemala's kindred desire for land reform led to covert overthrow of their domestic democratic governments in 1953 and 1954 respectively
Vietnam y el deficit como politica

the U.S. payments deficit stemmed entirely from foreign military spending, mainly for the Vietnam War but also for other U.S. military activities around the world... Just as World Wars I and II had bankrupted Europe
London Gold Pool collapses; dollar loses its gold anchor

Closing the gold window had been imminent since the London Gold Pool was disbanded in 1968 in response to the U.S. overseas military spending that had pushed the balance of payments into steadily deepening deficit
p. iii
Nixon termina patrón oro: dólar libre

in August 1971, President Nixon made the gold embargo official. The key-currency standard based on the dollar's convertibility into gold was dead. The U.S. Treasury-bill standard, based on dollar inconvertibility, was inaugurated
Connally: nuestra moneda, su problema

As Treasury Secretary John Connally said in September 1971, a month after the U.S. went off gold, its payments deficit was the world's problem. To America it was a means of funding its Cold War spending with other nation's credit
p. v
OPEP cuadruplica el precio del petroleo

To the OPEC economies, the inflation became a major reason prompting them to quadruple oil prices from late 1973 through early 1974. Gold prices soared to over $700 an ounce as U.S. monetary self-interest spurred a worldwide rise
El Consenso de Washington como doctrina

The Washington Consensus has called for a neoliberal wave of privatizations throughout the world since the 1980s, often financed by foreign debt, especially via U.S. and allied bank credit. This is the opposite policy
p. x
Acuerdos del Plaza humillan a Japon

The Plaza Accords of 1985, and the Louvre Accords the following year, obliged Japan's central bank to lower interest rates and inflate a bubble economy that burst in five years, leaving Japan a financial wreck
Disolución de la URSS y conquista financiera de Rusia

The result of the post-1980 U.S. economic decline and the post-1991 dissolution of the USSR is that instead of a conflict between Soviet Communism and American capitalism, today's primary conflict is between industrial and finance capitalism
p. x
Crisis asiatica y reciclaje forzado

Today, America's trade deficit is pumping dollars into the central banks of Asia and Europe, to be recycled into the U.S. capital markets and help inflate a sustained financial bubble... since the 1997 Asian crash
Invasion de Iraq y guerra de divisas

Similar coercion occurred vis-a-vis Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Iraq and Iran to buy U.S. arms with the dollar proceeds of their oil exports. An ideal scenario to U.S. eyes might have been one in which U.S. arms clients invaded
Crisis financiera y rescates a costa del Sur

In the wake of the post-2008 financial crisis, U.S. neoliberalism has mobilized the world's central banks to engage in quantitative easing to support stock and bond markets while not alleviating the austerity imposed by U.S-led financialization
Sanciones a Rusia tras Crimea
Economic sanctions against Russia were a logical extension of the United States pursuing its goal of an open world economy by isolating economies deemed potential rivals to U.S commercial interests
Guerra comercial de Trump y aranceles
President Trump's U.S. 25 percent steel tariff and 10 percent aluminum tariff. The effect seems to be driving Germany and other European countries out of the U.S. orbit
p. xi
Sanciones SWIFT y de-dolarizacion

China, Russia and other countries are moving to create alternative regional currency blocs so as to de-dollarize their trade and payments. America's response has been to impose punitive sanctions to deter such moves
